name: York
title: Holidays in York
intro: Medieval walls you can walk on, a vast Gothic minster, the Shambles and Viking history. Here's what York is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: York's medieval city walls with York Minster's towers rising behind

facts.label: Entry
facts.value: No passport checks within the UK

facts_note: UK and Irish citizens don't need a passport to travel within the UK, but airlines ask for photo ID. Most other visitors need an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA), so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May, June and September are the best months for walking the walls in mild weather. February brings the Jorvik Viking Festival, with battle re-enactments for half term. From mid November to late December, St Nicholas Fair fills the city with Christmas chalets. Summer is busy, and winters are cold but atmospheric.

things.name: York Minster
things.blurb: One of the biggest Gothic cathedrals in Europe. Climb the central tower's 275 steps for the view.

things.name: City walls
things.blurb: Walk the two-mile circuit of medieval walls, the most complete in England.

things.name: The Shambles
things.blurb: A crooked medieval street of overhanging timber buildings, now full of shops and cafés.

things.name: Jorvik Viking Centre
things.blurb: Ride through a rebuilt Viking street, sounds and smells included, on the spot where it was dug up.

things.name: National Railway Museum
things.blurb: The Flying Scotsman, Mallard and a Japanese bullet train, free to visit.

things.name: North York Moors
things.blurb: Steam trains, moorland and the seaside at Whitby are about an hour away.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in York?
faqs.answer: Two days covers the Minster, the walls, the Shambles and a museum or two. Add a day for Whitby or the Yorkshire Dales.

faqs.question: Is York good for children?
faqs.answer: Yes. Jorvik, the free National Railway Museum, the walls and the ghost walks all work well with children.

faqs.question: When is the York Christmas market?
faqs.answer: St Nicholas Fair usually runs from mid November until just before Christmas, in Parliament Street and around the Minster.

faqs.question: How do you get to York?
faqs.answer: Trains from London King's Cross take under two hours, and from Edinburgh about two and a half. Leeds Bradford is the nearest airport, and Manchester has more flights.
